newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico hopes to award rail concession in October.
newsitem.headline: Mexico hopes to award rail concession in October.

text.p: The Mexican government hopes to award the first of its rail concessions up for privatisation in October, a transportation official said on Wednesday.
Three groups are bidding on the so-called Chihuahua-Pacific line in northern Mexico, which runs through the spectacular Copper Canyon tourist attraction.

"On September 30 we are going to receive technical offers and 10 days later, we hope, the economic offers, when the assigning of the Chihuahua-Pacific route will be decided," Jorge Silberstein, technical secretary of the transportation ministry's privatization committee, told Reuters in an interview.

Silberstein identified the three finalists as groups led by Mexican shipping giant Transportacion Maritima Mexicana, the major Mexican construction firm Tribasa, and a joint venture among Itisa, Grupo Mexico and a company identified as South Oriente.
Silberstein said the Mexican firm Transporta Internacional was disqualified as a finalist for failing to report information about its investor group to the Federal Competition Commission (CFC).
